result.note: normal_open is the switch's state as the network was loaded (its normal state), open its state now. A tie joins two feeders: closing it restores supply across them (not checked against flows). Roles are inferred from the topology.

rating_mva.from: its current rating at the line's voltage

supply.from: inferred from the topology as switched now: the shortest route by number of branches from an external grid; the feeder is the first line after the last transformer on it

without_it.from: topology only: the buses that lose every connection to an external grid (no power flow run); the load is their demand at the network's current operating point
open_ties_that_could_restore: Line 14-8 | Bus 14 -> Bus 8 [L14] (switch S1, open at Bus 8)

assistant:
At **2000-01-01 00:00**, tripping **Line 2-3** cuts supply to 11 loads on the disconnected section: **Load R3, Load CI3, Load R4, Load R5, Load R6, Load CI7, Load R8, Load CI9, Load R10, Load CI10, and Load R11**. The contingency study reports **1.95 MW** of unsupplied load across buses 3–11.

The normally open tie identified as able to restore supply is **S1**, on **Line 14-8** (open at Bus 8). Closing it would reconnect the isolated section to the other feeder; the restoration path’s loading and protection suitability were not assessed here.

📋 Data source: measurements
